metaDescription: Six 2000 PSI class electric pressure washers compared on rated versus max PSI, GPM, motor, hose, wheels and warranty for patios, cars and decks.
expertTake: The Westinghouse ePX3500 is the pick for most homeowners, because it states a true 2000 rated PSI at 1.2 GPM, not just a max figure, and adds anti-tip wheels and a 3 year warranty. The Greenworks 2000 PSI is the best value pick, with a PWMA-rated 2000 PSI at 1.2 GPM and a simple on-board soap tank. The CRAFTSMAN CMEPW2100 is the best pick for movement, with 10 inch wheels. If you plan to strip paint, clean big concrete areas or run it for hours, skip this class and look at a gas washer.
introParagraphs: An electric pressure washer uses a motor to drive a small pump that forces water through a narrow nozzle, so a thin jet cuts through grime that a garden hose only wets. The 2000 PSI class is the sweet spot for cars, patio furniture, decks and fences. The trouble is that the pressure number printed on the box is often not the pressure you get at the nozzle.

This guide explains rated versus max pressure, why flow rate matters as much as pressure, how the pump and motor differ and what the hose, wheels and cord say about a machine. Start with the picks above for the short list, then read the reviews below to match a washer to your surfaces, your storage space and the jobs you do.

products.name: Westinghouse ePX3500 2000 Rated PSI Electric Pressure Washer
products.description:
The ePX3500 is the only machine in this lineup that states its rated pressure on the label rather than leading with a max figure. It delivers 2000 rated PSI at 1.2 rated GPM, with a max figure of 2500 PSI and 1.76 GPM at its lowest pressure. The rated numbers are the ones that describe sustained cleaning, and they place the washer at about 2,400 cleaning units, which is pressure times flow, the best single comparison between machines.

The hardware follows from that honesty. A pro style steel wand extends to 17.5 inches and takes quick connect nozzles at 0, 15 and 25 degrees plus a turbo and a soap applicator. A 25 foot nylon braided hose and a 20 ounce on-board soap tank round it out. The frame is low and stable, with four quick lock wheels and 360 degree steering, and it weighs 19 pounds. Against the Westinghouse WPX2300e, which lists 1900 rated PSI, it gives about 100 more rated PSI, and against the Greenworks 2000 PSI it matches the rated pressure and flow while adding anti-tipping design.

It carries a three year limited warranty with a nationwide support network, and the pump stops when you release the trigger, which saves energy and pump life. Ownership is light: use the soap tip to draw detergent, never run the pump dry, connect water before pulling the trigger, and drain and store it above freezing, since frozen water in a pump cracks it.
products.bestFor: Homeowners who want a clearly stated 2000 rated PSI machine with a stable frame and a three year warranty.
pros: States 2000 rated PSI at 1.2 GPM, not just a max figure
Low, anti-tipping frame with 360 degree steering wheels
Steel extendable wand takes quick connect nozzles
Three year limited warranty with nationwide support
cons: The 2500 max PSI headline overstates sustained pressure
Small 20 oz soap tank empties quickly on big jobs
Only 25 ft hose limits reach without moving the machine

products.name: Greenworks 2000 PSI 1.2 GPM Electric Pressure Washer

specList.label: Rating
specList.value: Rated in accordance with PWMA standards

specList.label: Energy saving
specList.value: Motor stops when trigger is released

products.description:
Greenworks keeps this machine simple. A 14 amp motor with a push button start drives a pump to 2000 PSI at 1.2 GPM, and the figures are rated in accordance with PWMA standards, the industry's test protocol for pressure washers. That matters because the number is meant to represent what the machine does, not a peak. It stops the motor when the trigger is released, which saves energy and extends pump and motor life.

An on-board soap tank lets you switch from rinsing to detergent just by changing to the soap tip, and the draw is automatic. Against the Westinghouse ePX3500 the Greenworks matches the pressure and flow, but it lacks the anti-tipping frame and the longer warranty, so it is the choice if you want the same sustained cleaning power for less. Compared with the CRAFTSMAN CMEPW2100, which lists 2100 max PSI at 1.2 GPM, the Greenworks gives a rated 2000 PSI, which is the more honest number.

It suits patio furniture, grills, walkways and vehicles, the medium duty work the maker lists. Ownership is light: no oil, no gas, no spark plug. Keep the inlet screen clean, flush detergent through the machine with clean water after soap use, and drain it before freezing weather. Check the warranty terms on the seller page when you buy, since the data we have does not state them.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a PWMA-rated 2000 PSI machine with a soap tank at a lower cost than the premium picks.
pros: Rated to PWMA standards at 2000 PSI and 1.2 GPM
Soap tank switches on with a nozzle change
Motor stops when the trigger is released to save wear
Push button start with no oil, gas or pull cord
cons: No stated anti-tip frame or hose reel
Warranty terms are not stated in the data we have
Medium duty only, not for paint stripping or big concrete

products.name: CRAFTSMAN CMEPW2100 2100 Max PSI Electric Pressure Washer
products.description:
The CRAFTSMAN is built around easy movement and storage. It lists 2100 max PSI at 1.2 GPM, a 25 foot kink-resistant hose, a 35 foot power cord and 10 inch wheels, the largest wheels in the lineup, which roll over gravel, steps and uneven yards better than small casters. Onboard storage holds the nozzles, hose, cord and wand, so the machine is a single piece when it is put away.

The number to read is the max PSI. Because it is a max, the sustained pressure will be lower, and with the flow at 1.2 GPM the machine sits in the same class as the Greenworks 2000 PSI. It is CETA certified, an industry certification of the performance claims, which helps credibility. Compared with the sibling CRAFTSMAN CMEPW1900, which is a similar design with 1900 max PSI and 8 inch wheels, the 2100 model gives more pressure and a larger wheel.

Ownership is routine electric washer care: use an integrated soap tank for detergents, flush the system with clean water after soap, drain it before storing and keep the hose coiled loosely so it does not kink. A GFCI protected outlet and an outdoor rated extension cord are a sensible habit. Check the warranty terms on the seller page before buying, since the data we have does not state them.
products.bestFor: Owners of larger yards with steps, gravel or uneven ground who want big wheels and a long cord and hose.
pros: Ten inch wheels roll over gravel and uneven ground
Thirty five foot cord and 25 ft hose extend reach
Onboard storage keeps wand, hose and nozzles organized
CETA certified performance claims
cons: The 2100 figure is a max, so sustained pressure is lower
Warranty terms are not stated in the data we have
No anti-tip design or foam cannon in the listing

products.name: Westinghouse WPX2300e 2300 Max PSI Induction Motor Pressure Washer
products.description:
This is the Westinghouse with the heavier build. It pairs a 120 V induction motor with an axial, three piston auto stop pump, a tough steel frame, 8 inch never-flat wheels and a 35 foot GFCI cord. Induction motors run cooler and quieter than the universal motors found on bargain washers, and they tend to last longer under repeated start stop use, which is how a pressure washer is really used.

The rated figures are 1900 PSI at 1.2 GPM with a max of 2300 PSI and 1.76 GPM at its lowest pressure. That puts it about 100 rated PSI behind the ePX3500's 2000, so it sits slightly below the nominal 2000 PSI class, though its max figure rounds to higher. It includes a 0.42 gallon soap tank, a 25 foot hose, five quick connect nozzles and M22 fittings that accept surface cleaners, undercarriage cleaners and foam cannons.

The three year limited warranty applies. Ownership is straightforward: connect the water and purge air before starting, keep the inlet filter clean, flush the soap system and drain the pump before freezing weather. The heavier steel frame also makes it less portable than the 19 pound ePX3500, so choose it for a garage or driveway home base rather than carrying it up stairs.
products.bestFor: Owners who want a durable induction motor, accessory compatibility and a three year warranty and do not need to carry the machine.
pros: Induction motor runs cooler and quieter than universal motors
Axial three piston pump with auto stop
M22 fittings accept surface cleaners and foam cannons
Three year limited warranty
cons: Rated 1900 PSI, slightly below the ePX3500
Heavier steel frame is harder to carry
Max PSI headline can mislead about sustained pressure

products.name: VEVOR 2000 PSI 1.76 GPM Electric Pressure Washer with Hose Reel

specList.label: Accessories
specList.value: 4 metal nozzles, foam cannon, 500 ml soap bottle

specList.label: Safety
specList.value: Press-type trigger lock, thermal cutoff, TSS pump stop

products.description:
The VEVOR pitches a bigger flow number than anything else in the 2000 PSI class: 1.76 GPM against 1.2 GPM for the Greenworks and Westinghouse ePX3500. That is a bold claim, and it needs care: the listing does not separate a rated figure from a max figure the way Westinghouse does, so treat both numbers as peaks until the owner's manual says otherwise. If the flow figure is true at 2000 PSI, the cleaning power would be about 3,500 cleaning units, well above the 2,400 of the rated machines, but a 1500 watt motor on a household circuit makes that hard to believe.

Its practical feature is the built-in hose reel, which keeps the 20 foot hose coiled and kink-free, plus four quick connect metal nozzles, a foam cannon and a 500 ml soap bottle. A Total Stop System turns the pump off when the trigger is released, the gun has a press-type lock, and a thermal cutoff stops the motor if it overheats. The unit is ETL certified, and the maker recommends not running it for more than 3 hours at a time.

The body is plastic with two small wheels, so it is a lighter, less rugged machine than the Westinghouse WPX2300e. Ownership means checking fittings for leaks, flushing the soap system, draining the pump before freezing and keeping the machine out of the sun. Check the warranty terms before buying.
products.bestFor: Buyers who value a hose reel and a bundled foam cannon, and accept a less established brand.
pros: Built-in hose reel keeps the 20 ft hose tidy
Foam cannon, four metal nozzles and soap bottle included
Thermal cutoff and trigger lock add safety
ETL certified
cons: Flow and pressure figures are not split into rated and max
Plastic body and two small wheels feel less rugged
Warranty terms are not stated in the data we have

products.name: CRAFTSMAN CMEPW1900 1900 Max PSI Electric Pressure Washer
products.description:
The CMEPW1900 is the lighter duty sibling of the CMEPW2100. It lists 1900 max PSI at 1.2 GPM, with the same 25 foot kink-resistant hose, 35 foot cord, integrated soap tank and onboard storage, but on 8 inch wheels instead of 10. The flow is identical to the 2100 model, so the practical difference is a bit less pressure and smaller wheels.

It belongs in this lineup as a lower-pressure option for people who clean cars, outdoor furniture, grills and light concrete, where less pressure is a feature because high pressure can etch paint, strip wood grain and damage soft siding. With a max of 1900 PSI the sustained figure is lower, so think of it as a light duty machine. It is CETA certified, which supports the performance claim.

Ownership matches the other electric washers: flush the soap system, keep the hose coiled loosely, drain the pump before freezing and use a GFCI protected outlet. Compared with the Westinghouse ePX3500, it gives up rated pressure disclosure and the three year warranty, and compared with the CMEPW2100 it gives up the larger wheels. Check the warranty terms on the seller page before buying.
products.bestFor: Owners who mostly wash cars, furniture and light surfaces and want a lower pressure Craftsman with storage and a long cord.
pros: Lower pressure is gentler on paint, wood and siding
Thirty five foot cord and 25 ft hose give long reach
Onboard storage holds wand, hose and nozzles
CETA certified performance claims
cons: Smaller 8 in wheels roll less easily than the 2100 model
The 1900 figure is a max, so sustained pressure is lower
Warranty terms are not stated in the data we have

buyingCriteria.explanation: Max PSI is the peak the pump can reach, usually at the lowest flow and for a moment, while rated PSI is the pressure the machine holds in use. The Westinghouse ePX3500 lists 2500 max and 2000 rated PSI, the WPX2300e lists 2300 max and 1900 rated, and the Greenworks lists 2000 PSI under PWMA standards. A washer that states only a max, like the CRAFTSMAN CMEPW2100 at 2100, will deliver less in practice. Compare rated figures where they exist.

Pressure breaks dirt loose, and flow carries it away, so the product of pressure and flow, called cleaning units, is a better yardstick than either number alone. The Greenworks and the Westinghouse ePX3500 both come to about 2,400 cleaning units at 2000 PSI and 1.2 GPM. The VEVOR claims 1.76 GPM at 2000 PSI, which would be higher, but it does not split rated from max. More flow cleans faster, up to what a household circuit can power.

A universal motor is cheap and loud, while an induction motor runs cooler, quieter and tends to last longer. The Westinghouse WPX2300e uses an induction motor with an axial three piston pump. The pump itself is the heart of the machine, and axial pumps on this class are usually maintenance free but cannot be repaired. Check whether the pump stops when the trigger is released, as the Greenworks and VEVOR do.

A short hose and cord mean moving the machine more often. The CRAFTSMAN models pair a 25 foot hose with a 35 foot cord, the Westinghouse WPX2300e has a 35 foot GFCI cord and a 25 foot hose, and the VEVOR has a 20 foot hose on a reel. A kink-resistant hose lasts longer. Use an outdoor rated extension cord only if you must, and keep it short.

Small plastic wheels catch on edges and tip. The CRAFTSMAN CMEPW2100 has 10 inch wheels, the Westinghouse WPX2300e has 8 inch never-flat wheels, and the Westinghouse ePX3500 has four quick lock wheels with an anti-tipping frame at 19 pounds. Choose by where you will use it: stairs and gravel favor large wheels, a garage floor favors a compact, stable base.

More pressure is not better for every job. A 0 degree nozzle can gouge wood and strip paint, while a 40 degree nozzle is gentle enough for cars. Most washers here include 0, 15, 25 and 40 degree nozzles or a turbo nozzle. Start with a wide nozzle and move closer, test an out-of-sight patch and keep the wand moving.

specDecoder.meaning: The highest pressure the pump can reach, often at the lowest flow. Sustained pressure during cleaning is lower.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Westinghouse ePX3500's 2500 max is 500 PSI above its 2000 rated figure, so a max-only listing hides a large gap.

specDecoder.meaning: The pressure the machine delivers in normal use at its rated flow. It is the figure to use when comparing washers.
specDecoder.watchFor: Rated numbers should come with a standard such as PWMA, as on the Greenworks listing.

specDecoder.meaning: Gallons per minute, the water flow. It sets how fast dirt is carried away and how quickly a surface is rinsed.
specDecoder.watchFor: A max GPM at the lowest pressure, like Westinghouse's 1.76, is not the flow at rated pressure, which is 1.2.

specDecoder.meaning: Pressure multiplied by flow. It gives a single number for cleaning power, such as 2,400 for 2000 PSI at 1.2 GPM.
specDecoder.watchFor: Make sure you multiply rated figures, not max ones.

specDecoder.meaning: Industry bodies that set testing or certification standards for pressure washers. They add credibility to the numbers.
specDecoder.watchFor: A certification does not guarantee a long warranty. Read the warranty terms separately.

howWeEvaluated.title: Rated versus advertised output
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared rated PSI and GPM against max figures, such as 2000 rated against 2500 max on the Westinghouse ePX3500. Machines that state rated output or a PWMA standard ranked higher than max-only listings.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning power
howWeEvaluated.description: We calculated cleaning units from rated pressure and flow, about 2,400 for the Greenworks and ePX3500 and about 2,280 for the WPX2300e. We treated the VEVOR's 1.76 GPM at 2000 PSI with caution.

howWeEvaluated.title: Motor, pump and durability
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared motor types and pump designs, with the WPX2300e's induction motor and three piston axial pump at the top, and noted auto stop features and thermal protection.

howWeEvaluated.title: Handling and reach
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared wheel sizes, weights, hose and cord lengths: 10 inch wheels on the CMEPW2100, 8 inch never-flat on the WPX2300e, a 25 foot hose and 35 foot cord on the CRAFTSMAN models, and a reel on the VEVOR.

howWeEvaluated.title: Warranty and support
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated warranty terms, three years on the Westinghouse models, and flagged machines without stated terms in the data we have. Certifications like CETA and PWMA were noted as signs of credibility.

howToChoose.intro: The jobs you do decide how much pressure you need.

rows: Large yard with steps or gravel
PWMA rated and a soap tank

howToChoose.intro: Understanding the label is the main trick in this category.

cards.label: Rated
cards.text: Rated PSI and GPM describe what the machine delivers in use, tested to a standard. The Westinghouse ePX3500 (2000 PSI), the WPX2300e (1900 PSI) and the Greenworks 2000 PSI (PWMA) fall in this group.

cards.label: Max only
cards.text: Max PSI is a peak figure and the sustained pressure is lower. The CRAFTSMAN CMEPW2100 (2100), the CMEPW1900 (1900) and the VEVOR (2000, unsplit) fall in this group.

howToChoose.note: Choose the rated machines if you want predictable results. Treat max-only listings as a bit lower than they read.

howToChoose.intro: Where you keep and use the machine is the second axis.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A wide fan nozzle and enough flow to rinse quickly, since too much pressure on wood raises the grain and damages the surface. About 1900 to 2000 rated PSI is enough for patios and decks when you keep a safe distance. Test on a hidden spot.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Westinghouse ePX3500 at 2000 rated PSI and 1.2 GPM is the best match, with the Greenworks 2000 PSI close behind at a lower cost. The CRAFTSMAN CMEPW1900 is a gentler choice for softwood decks.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want clearly stated rated output, an anti-tipping frame, a three year warranty or an induction motor. The Westinghouse ePX3500 and the WPX2300e are the picks.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You wash cars and furniture a few times a year. The Greenworks 2000 PSI or the CRAFTSMAN CMEPW1900 give enough pressure at a lower cost.

howToChoose.note: If you strip paint, clean large areas of concrete or run the washer for hours, a gas pressure washer is the better tool.

maintenance.why: Debris from the water supply blocks the pump inlet and starves it of water. A clogged screen reduces pressure and can damage the pump.
Dried detergent clogs siphon tubes and fittings. Run clean water through the machine for a minute.

maintenance.task: Drain the pump before freezing weather
maintenance.why: Water left inside a pump expands as it freezes and cracks the housing. Disconnect hoses and run the trigger until the water stops.

maintenance.task: Check hose and fittings for leaks
maintenance.why: A leaking fitting wastes pressure. A cracked hose is a safety hazard under pressure.
Without water, the pump overheats in seconds. Connect water and squeeze the trigger to purge air before starting the motor.

faq.q: Is 2000 PSI enough for a driveway?
faq.a: For light to moderate stains and routine cleaning, yes, especially with a turbo nozzle. It will take longer than a gas washer at 3000 PSI and above, and tough oil stains need a pre-treatment. For large areas, flow rate matters as much as pressure.

faq.q: How much should I budget for a 2000 PSI pressure washer?
faq.a: Electric washers in this class cost less than gas models and range from budget to premium within a few tiers. A longer warranty, rated output and sturdier build sit at the premium end. Add the cost of a surface cleaner or foam cannon if you want one.

faq.q: How long do electric pressure washers last?
faq.a: With care, many last several seasons. The pump is the part that fails, usually from freezing or running dry. Drain the machine before cold weather and never run it without water.

faq.q: What is the difference between max PSI and rated PSI?
faq.a: Max PSI is a peak the pump reaches briefly, usually at low flow. Rated PSI is the pressure the machine holds in use. A washer listed at 2500 max can be rated at only 2000.

faq.q: Is a pressure washer safe to use?
faq.a: Treat the jet as a cutting tool. Never point it at people, pets or yourself, wear eye protection and closed shoes, and use a GFCI protected outlet. Keep the nozzle at least a foot from the surface at first.

faq.q: Can I use hot water in an electric pressure washer?
faq.a: Most electric washers are for cold water only. Check the maximum inlet temperature in the manual. The Greenworks 3000 PSI model lists 104 F as its maximum inlet temperature, for example.
